scope: Reviewed word/phrase meanings of Śrīdhara Svāmī's Sanskrit commentary, NOT Bhāgavatam-verse synonyms. Only the entries explicitly listed are complete; the remaining verses are not represented as translated word-for-word.

pairs: delight in the accounts of Hari
a taste for it does not arise
with the words ‘of one eager to hear’
through attendance upon holy places of merit
service of great souls comes about
while describing their being causes of misfortune
ब्रूहि यद् वा, विपर्ययम् इत्य् अस्योत्तरम् आह
he answers the earlier request beginning ‘Tell [me] what, instead, is the opposite’
with three verses beginning ‘Things to be heard,’ and so on
of those attached to their homes
of those engaged in household life, glossed through the root medh
of those involved in its five household sources of injury
the verb medh has the meaning ‘to injure’
entries.note: A numbered footnote supplies a separate illustrative verse about the five household sources of injury; it is not silently attributed to Śrīdhara's own prose.

pairs: he describes it as not fit to abandon
the demonstrative ‘this’ is used because he is present in the mind
Duryodhana, the chief of the Pauravas
he entered [the Pāṇḍavas' house] even without being invited
having left her husband, she went
having angrily rebuked him at the sacrifice
it is told that she abandoned her body
तदा सा सती द्विधा आस बभूव
Satī was then of two minds
her movement was like that of a swing
